clue.text: Sid and I upset by scorn

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over and disordered, so the letters before it are rearranged

blocks.note: the name, the joining word and the pronoun taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Two friends are hurt by someone's contempt.
explanation.definitionFit: Disdain and scorn are both nouns for open contempt felt toward someone thought unworthy.

clue.text: Novice has to pray inside

blocks.note: to pray in the old sense is to ask earnestly, to plead
inside as an adjective means interior

explanation.surface: A new recruit to a religious order must say prayers indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inside' looks like a container signal, but here it simply supplies a synonym tacked on at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A novice is someone just starting out at something, which is exactly what a learner at the start is.

clue.text: Put an end to spirit North of the Border

blocks.note: first meaning: to quash or stamp out a rumour or plan
second meaning: the whisky distilled in Scotland

explanation.walkthrough: North of the Border is the British way of saying Scotland, the land beyond the English border.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means to quash or suppress; as a noun it names the whisky distilled in Scotland.

clue.text: Best street to go in is the widest

indicators.note: one word is told to go in, so it is placed within the letters of another

blocks.note: taken as written
a road is a street

explanation.surface: Advice on which avenue to enter: the widest one is the finest.
explanation.definitionFit: Broad and wide are synonyms, so the superlative of one matches the superlative of the other.

clue.text: Material an accountant left with one firm

blocks.note: CA is a chartered accountant
L is the usual abbreviation for left
the Roman numeral for one
Co is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: Documents belonging to a bookkeeper who has quit to join a single company.
explanation.walkthrough: CA, chartered accountant, is a British professional title.
explanation.definitionFit: Calico is a plain-woven cotton cloth, so it is a kind of fabric or textile.

clue.text: Walter edited the part that's changed

indicators.note: only a part of the following words is wanted, a run of letters lying within them

blocks.note: the letters run from the second letter of the name to the middle of the verb

explanation.surface: Walter revised the section of the text that was amended.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are past participles meaning made different or modified in some way.

clue.text: Since the Parisian dropped in, it's quiet

indicators.note: something dropped in falls inside, so one piece sits within the letters of another

blocks.note: taken as written
le is French for the, as a Parisian would say it

explanation.surface: Ever since a Frenchman came by unannounced, things have gone calm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dropped in' reads as a visit, but it tells you to insert one piece into the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Quiet as a noun means a lack of noise, which is the same as stillness without sound.

clue.text: A down-trodden machine operator

blocks.note: surface reading: an oppressed factory worker
setter's reading: literally pressed down by the foot to work a machine such as a sewing machine

explanation.walkthrough: 'Down-trodden' sounds like oppressed, but read literally it means trodden down, the way a foot pedal is worked.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a foot pedal that drives a wheel on a sewing machine or lathe, operated by pressing with the foot.

clue.text: Twenty pieces of timber seen at cricket grounds

definitions.note: a description of where the things are found, standing for the plural noun

blocks.note: a score is a set of twenty
boards are flat lengths of sawn wood

explanation.surface: Twenty planks of wood stacked up beside cricket pitches.
explanation.definitionFit: Every cricket ground has large displays showing runs and wickets so spectators can follow the match.

clue.text: A pile of snow cut loose

blocks.note: taken as written
a drift is a bank of snow heaped by wind

explanation.surface: A heap of snow breaks free and slides away.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat that has been cut loose floats freely without mooring, unanchored and drifting with the current.

clue.text: Music-maker wanting wine to take in

indicators.note: to take something on board is to hold it, so one word swallows the other

blocks.note: claret is red Bordeaux wine
taken as written

explanation.surface: A musician who wants a drink of wine to swallow.
explanation.definitionFit: A clarinet is a woodwind instrument, and an instrument is something that produces music.

clue.text: Learner is taken in by family baker

indicators.note: being taken in by something means being held within it, so one piece sits inside another

blocks.note: kin are one's relatives
L is the learner plate on British cars

explanation.surface: A trainee is deceived by the relatives of the local bread-maker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Baker' looks like a person, but it is the oven that bakes pottery and bricks.
explanation.definitionFit: A kiln is a furnace used for firing pottery or bricks, so it literally bakes them hard.

clue.text: Engines produce this; something you ride might

blocks.note: a horse is an animal you ride
might as a noun means strength

explanation.surface: Motors generate this output, as might a mount you sit on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Might' looks like a verb, but it is the noun meaning strength.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the unit in which the output of an engine is measured, originally pegged to what a draught animal could pull.

clue.text: Inhibit poor in another form of ban

indicators.note: putting words into another form means reshaping them, so their letters are rearranged

blocks.note: both words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Restraining the needy is just another version of exclusion.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitalised word was the US ban on alcohol from 1920 to 1933.
explanation.definitionFit: A prohibition is an official order forbidding something, which is exactly what a ban is.

clue.text: Holy building was in debt

blocks.note: a hall is a large building or room
owed means had money due to someone

explanation.surface: A church that was struggling to pay its bills.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hallowed has been made sacred or consecrated, so it is revered as holy.

clue.text: Away from work stopped getting insulted

blocks.note: someone off is not at work
ended means finished or stopped

explanation.surface: Someone laid off from their job feels slighted.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone insulted feels hurt or affronted, the usual meaning of having taken offence.

clue.text: Searched for food for the elderly?

blocks.note: taken as written
the aged are old people

explanation.surface: A volunteer shopping for groceries on behalf of pensioners.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the words for the elderly are split and read literally.
explanation.definitionFit: To forage is to hunt about for provisions, so the past tense fits looking for something to eat.

clue.text: Having left instructions in case one becomes late!

definitions.text: Having left instructions in case one becomes late!

blocks.clueFragment: Having left instructions in case one becomes late
blocks.note: surface reading: leaving a note in case you are delayed
setter's reading: dies, becoming 'the late' someone, so the instructions are a will

explanation.walkthrough: Late suggests tardy, but it means deceased, as in 'the late Mr Smith'.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who dies having made a valid will is described in law by this term, the opposite of intestate.

clue.text: Seek advice about tan from specialist

indicators.note: turned about, the word's letters are moved around into a new order

blocks.note: to consult is to seek advice
taken as written

explanation.surface: Ask a dermatologist for guidance about your suntan.
explanation.definitionFit: A consultant is a senior hospital doctor who is an expert in one branch of medicine.

clue.text: Part of railway sign I'd damaged

indicators.note: something damaged is broken up, so the preceding letters are rearranged

blocks.note: both words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A railway signal that someone admits to vandalising.
explanation.definitionFit: A siding is a short stretch of track off the main line where trains are parked.

clue.text: Sunburnt man embraces Ann

indicators.note: to embrace is to wrap one's arms around, so one name surrounds the other

blocks.note: Ted is a man's name
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sunburnt fellow hugs his friend Ann.
explanation.definitionFit: Skin that is browned by exposure to the sun is said to be sunburnt in the older sense of the word.

clue.text: Nothing to pay, so charge is about right!

indicators.note: one thing being about another means it is around it, enclosing it

blocks.note: a fee is a charge
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: No payment needed, so the fee is fair enough!
explanation.definitionFit: Something that costs nothing is offered gratis, with no payment required from anyone.

clue.text: It's amusing returning and going in to see host

indicators.note: a word that is returning goes back the way it came, so it is read from end to start
going in means entering, so one word is put inside another

blocks.note: droll means wryly funny
taken as written

explanation.surface: A funny thing happens when you come back and go inside to visit your host.
explanation.definitionFit: A landlord who keeps an inn or pub is the host who welcomes and serves the guests.

clue.text: Number and name, yet in different order

indicators.note: putting letters in a different order is exactly what rearranging them means

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for name
both words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A list of numbers and names that has been put into the wrong sequence.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'in' belongs to the letters being rearranged, not to the order signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninety is a cardinal number, nine times ten, so it is an example of a number.

clue.text: Me and the Queen wander aimlessly

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen's royal cipher

explanation.surface: I go strolling about without purpose alongside Her Majesty.
explanation.definitionFit: To meander is to follow a winding course, like a river, roaming without a fixed direction.

clue.text: Abandons infertile regions

blocks.note: first meaning: leaves someone in the lurch, a verb
second meaning: barren arid lands such as the Sahara, a plural noun

explanation.surface: Someone forsakes barren land.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means walks out on a duty or person; as a plural noun it names arid wastelands.
